summary: This standards-track memo defines a DHCPv6 option for giving a client a list of SNTP server addresses. This lets a client learn which time servers to use as part of its automatic configuration.

plainLanguage.summary: This DHCPv6 option gives a client IPv6 addresses of SNTP servers to use for time synchronization. The client treats the list as ordered.

questions: how does dhcpv6 provide time servers
what is the dhcpv6 sntp option
how does dhcpv6 provide sntp servers
why should dhcpv6 be authenticated for time servers
subtitle: A DHCPv6 option that gives clients an ordered list of IPv6 SNTP server addresses.

tldr.problem: DHCPv6 clients need a way to learn which SNTP servers are available for time synchronization.
tldr.mechanism: Option 31 carries one or more IPv6 server addresses, each 16 octets, in a list clients must treat as ordered.
tldr.outcome: Clients can receive IPv6 SNTP server information through DHCPv6, but the RFC recommends authenticated DHCPv6 to guard against rogue servers.

today: RFC 4075 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the Option Supplies
sections.content:
The SNTP servers option provides a list of one or more IPv6 addresses of SNTP servers available to the client. Clients use them to synchronize their system time to standard time servers.

The option covers only servers reachable using IPv6. The RFC points to RFC 2132 for the DHCP option used to configure IPv4 SNTP servers and does not specify dual-stack configuration.
sections.plainLanguage: The option gives a client addresses for time servers reachable over IPv6. It does not define how a client should combine IPv4 and IPv6 server configuration.

sections.title: Option Format and Placement
sections.content:
OPTION_SNTP_SERVERS has code 31. Its data contains IPv6 server addresses, and the option length must be a multiple of 16 octets. Clients MUST treat the addresses as an ordered list; a server MAY list them in decreasing order of preference.

The option may appear only in Solicit, Advertise, Request, Renew, Rebind, Information-Request, and Reply messages. Receivers SHOULD ignore it in other messages.
sections.plainLanguage: The option is a list of IPv6 addresses, each 16 octets long. The client uses them in the order sent by the server.

sections.title: Rogue SNTP Servers
sections.content:
An intruder DHCPv6 server could direct a client to a rogue SNTP server and cause incorrect time synchronization. The RFC notes that inaccurate time can affect security algorithms and timestamp-based replay protection.

To avoid attacks through the option, the DHCPv6 client SHOULD use authenticated DHCPv6.
sections.plainLanguage: A rogue server could provide an untrusted time-server address. The RFC recommends authenticating DHCPv6 messages to reduce this risk.
